scenes.line2: How do they speed up queries?
scenes.say: Why do indexes matter in SQL, and how do they actually speed up your queries?

scenes.label: B-tree
scenes.say: B-tree indexes are the default. They make searching and sorting data much faster.

rows.b: Contains all columns needed for query

scenes.say: Composite indexes cover several columns, but order is key. Covering indexes include every column your query needs, so the database can skip the table and use only the index.

scenes.code:
CREATE INDEX idx_emp_dept_salary
ON employees(department_id, salary);
scenes.say: Here's how you create a composite index on department ID and salary. The column order should match your most common WHERE or ORDER BY clauses.

scenes.question: Should you index every column?
scenes.wrong: Yes, more indexes are always better.
scenes.right: No. Too many indexes slow down writes and waste space.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: should you index every column? No way. Too many indexes slow down inserts and updates, and waste storage, especially on columns with few unique values.
